     1	# SPEC-039 — Paged KV / paged-attention engine
     2	
     3	Version: v0.1.6
     4	Status: draft (normative design). v0.1.6 lets a retained or positive-cache-credit
     5	hybrid request batch only where the SPEC-038 FR-CB10 accepted tuple covering it
     6	records `cached_turns_accepted` (the SPEC-038 AC-26 recurrent-handoff proof).
     7	v0.1.5 names how the FR-PKV13 overhead
     8	ceiling gates real traffic: through SPEC-038 FR-CB10 acceptance coverage bound
     9	to the measured runtime revision. v0.1.4 admits only the measured Qwen3.6
    10	mixed layout for first-turn batching: recurrent Mamba state remains row-local
    11	and only full-attention KV is paged. It does not authorize sliding-window
    12	attention or retained hybrid cross-turn state. v0.1.3 clarifies that gather-feeds-SDPA is
    13	the parity/correctness scaffold and default fail-safe proof path, not by
    14	itself a production-throughput claim for continuous batching; real serving
    15	enablement must pass the FR-PKV13 overhead ceiling and SPEC-038 real-serving
    16	gate. v0.1.2 admits `gpt_oss` as the first non-Qwen/Llama paged-KV family only
    17	through config-derived family identity plus the same per-model runtime
    18	exact-parity and batched-isolation measurement gates; other catalog families
    19	remain fail-closed until their own family fixtures are added. v0.1.1 clarified
    20	FR-PKV12 / AC-13: the attach-class probe evaluates the paged path's cache with
    21	the serve memory cap removed (`maxKVSize = nil`), so a full-context model that
    22	is `RotatingKVCache` only because the serve path caps KV for memory attaches to
    23	paged mode (the block pool bounds memory), while a genuine sliding-window model
    24	stays fail-safe. IMPL lands with this revision.
    25	Owner: provider runtime / inference engine
    26	Decision source: `docs/research/RESEARCH_232_ADDENDUM_PAGED_REDECISION_2026-07-29.md` plus the verified spike sequence `SPIKE_PAGED_ATTN_PHASE0_RESULT_2026-07-29.md` (`e5ded571`), `SPIKE_PAGED_ATTN_PHASE2_RESULT_2026-07-29.md` (`acc30b1e`), and `SPIKE_PAGED_ATTN_PHASE3_MOE_RESULT_2026-07-29.md` (`da21af53`).
    27	Audit history: three-lane codex SPEC audit (code / security / architect). Convergence and any carried LOW/INFO findings are recorded in the SPEC PR body and `audits/2026-07-29/SPEC-039-rN-audit.md`.
    28	
    29	## 1. Purpose and scope
    30	
    31	Define the provider-local paged KV cache and paged-attention engine that gives
    32	a Mac a **correctness-preserving paged KV residency** layout for its inference
    33	engine. This is **memory-servability** infrastructure: it changes KV residency
    34	and memory layout inside the provider inference engine, not buyer-visible
    35	billing, receipts, request schemas, model identity, or settlement.
    36	
    37	**Scope of the v0.1 claim (proven vs deferred).** v0.1 claims only
    38	correctness-preserving paged *residency*: KV is stored in non-contiguous
    39	physical blocks and gathered back into logical order before attention. The
    40	v0.1 default **gather-feeds-SDPA** mode (FR-PKV3) materializes a transient
    41	**contiguous** K/V copy per attention op before calling stock SDPA, so v0.1
    42	does **not** claim an attention-time peak-memory reduction; that peak-memory
    43	win requires the fully-fused paged-attention op, which is deferred (out of
    44	scope below; FR-PKV3). Framed honestly: **fp16 KV at batch size 1 is the
    45	correctness-proven foundation of this engine, not its servability payoff.** The
    46	throughput payoff comes from continuous batching (SPEC-038) sharing one paged
    47	pool across rows; the peak-memory payoff comes from quantized KV (future). Both
    48	are built on top of the exact-parity correctness this SPEC proves. The
    49	servability envelope this residency layout unlocks over the stock contiguous
    50	path — which model/context sizes fit on the 32 GB live-30B envelope that stock
    51	cannot — is a normative define-and-record obligation (FR-PKV13), not a v0.1
    52	performance claim.
    53	
    54	**Serving-path honesty.** This SPEC deliberately separates three surfaces:
    55	(1) the **parity scaffold**, where gather-feeds-SDPA proves block tables,
    56	logical ordering, allocator invariants, descriptor admission, and exact fp16
    57	parity; (2) a **production serving path**, which may consume the same
    58	descriptor, allocator, block-table handle, and FR-PKV10 materialize/retain
    59	primitives but MUST pass the recorded overhead ceiling and SPEC-038 packaged
    60	serving gate before real traffic; and (3) a future **fully-fused or
    61	block-aware paged-attention path**, which is the performance class used by
    62	mature paged-attention systems but is explicitly out of scope until a later
    63	SPEC/IMPL revision. A gather-every-step path that is correct but too slow is
    64	valid proof evidence; it is not sufficient production enable evidence.
    65	
    66	The v0.1 engine is additive on macprovider's pinned production stack,
    67	`mlx-swift-lm 3.31.4` -> `mlx-swift 0.31.4`. It MUST NOT require a fork of
    68	`mlx` or `mlx-swift` for the default path. The verified non-forking injection
    69	surface is a `PagedKVCache` conforming to `mlx-swift-lm`'s public `KVCache`
    70	protocol and passed through `model(_:cache:)`, so the existing model attention
    71	modules continue to apply RoPE, GQA/MQA grouping, and causal masking.
    72	
    73	This SPEC stands alone. It is useful at batch size 1 because paging changes KV
    74	residency and gives the provider an explicit, hard-bounded KV pool plus the
    75	consumer-facing block-table primitives (FR-PKV10) that SPEC-024 cross-turn
    76	cache reuse and SPEC-038 continuous batching consume. SPEC-038 continuous
    77	batching is a consumer of this engine, not a prerequisite.
    78	
    79	In scope for v0.1:
    80	
    81	- A provider-owned `PagedKVCache` for the production fp16 KV path.
    82	- Fixed-size physical KV blocks, per-sequence block tables, and a Swift block
    83	  allocator with allocation, free-list, eviction, and reclaim semantics.
    84	- A custom Metal kernel registered through public `MLXFast.metalKernel`,
    85	  used as the v0.1 parity/fail-safe scaffold to gather paged, non-contiguous
    86	  KV into logical order before feeding stock
    87	  `MLXFast.scaledDotProductAttention`.
    88	- Exact greedy-argmax parity gates against the stock contiguous fp16 path on
    89	  dense and MoE models.
    90	- Default-off, provider-local activation with fail-safe fallback to the stock
    91	  contiguous cache path.
    92	- Deliberate packaging of the MLX `default.metallib` resource required by
    93	  Metal-backed MLX execution.
    94	
    95	Out of scope for v0.1:
    96	
    97	- Any change to LOCKED SPEC-015 receipts, SPEC-024 cache billing semantics,
    98	  SPEC-005 billing arithmetic, buyer API response schemas, or settlement.
    99	- Any buyer-visible receipt, usage, or model identity field identifying paged
   100	  KV, block tables, kernel mode, or allocator state.
   101	- Paged **quantized** KV. `kvBits` is a distinct numerical surface and needs
   102	  its own path targeting `QuantizedKVCacheProtocol` /
   103	  `quantizedScaledDotProductAttention`.
   104	- A fully-fused paged-attention op replacing SDPA. The spike proved numerical
   105	  feasibility at production dimensions, but installing it requires a light
   106	  `mlx-swift-lm` fork of internal attention/helper code and is optional
   107	  future work.
   108	- Cross-provider or **cross-conversation** block sharing, global
   109	  content-addressed KV deduplication, or buyer-controlled block residency.
   110	  This exclusion is scoped to sharing blocks *between distinct conversations*
   111	  and to buyer-directed residency control. It does **not** exclude
   112	  **same-conversation** retain-and-reattach of a sequence's own blocks across
   113	  turns, nor materializing a sequence's own block table into a standalone
   114	  contiguous cache: those are the normative FR-PKV10 consumer primitives that
   115	  keep SPEC-024 cross-turn cache reuse eligible and are explicitly in scope.
   116	- Any cross-buyer, cross-account, global-prefix, salted-prefix, or
   117	  content-addressed prefix-sharing policy. A future broader sharing design MUST
   118	  specify tenant/account scope, salt/key derivation, privacy disclosure,
   119	  receipt/billing attribution, purge semantics, and cache-hit observability
   120	  before any implementation can serve real traffic.
   121	- Continuous-batching scheduling, admission, row lifecycle, per-request
   122	  accounting under a shared forward, and MoE expert dispatch under batching
   123	  (SPEC-038 territory).
   124	- Runtime offload to SSD/remote memory, LRU eviction policy under multi-request
   125	  pressure, priority-aware cache eviction, preemptive evict-and-recompute, and
   126	  disaggregated prefill/decode cache transfer. FR-PKV2 exposes the allocator
   127	  mechanism; these policies are future SPEC-038/SPEC-039 work.
   128	
   129	## 2. Dependencies and authority
   130	
   131	- **SPEC-001** — provider binary/config surface. This SPEC consumes provider
   132	  configuration and packaging authority without changing the wire protocol.
   133	- **SPEC-010** — model catalog identity. Paged residency MUST preserve the
   134	  served `model_sha256`, tokenizer identity, and model/cache compatibility
   135	  envelope.
   136	- **SPEC-015** — LOCKED receipts. Untouched; paged KV MUST NOT add or alter
   137	  any receipt field.
   138	- **SPEC-024** — provider prefix-cache billing isolation. Untouched; paged KV
   139	  changes residency/layout only and MUST preserve `cached_prompt_tokens`
   140	  computation wherever SPEC-024 reuse is otherwise eligible.
   141	- **SPEC-037** — KV survival across restarts. SPEC-039 **exposes** paged
   142	  layout metadata that a SPEC-037 implementation **MAY** consume if paged KV
   143	  becomes the resident in-memory layout; the decision whether SPEC-037 MUST
   144	  consume the paged layout (vs. keeping its serial layout flag-isolated from
   145	  persistence, SPEC-037 §8) belongs to the SPEC-037 owner, not to this SPEC
   146	  (FR-PKV9).
   147	- **SPEC-038** — continuous batching. SPEC-038 consumes this engine when it
   148	  needs per-sequence block tables under a shared scheduler; SPEC-039 MUST NOT
   149	  depend on SPEC-038.
   150	
   300	does not retroactively turn gather-feeds-SDPA into a performance claim.
   301	
   302	A **fully-fused paged-attention op** MAY be added later for maximum
   303	performance. That extension MAY require a light `mlx-swift-lm` fork because
   304	the relevant attention modules/helpers are internal. It MUST NOT require an
   305	`mlx` core fork. A fused-op implementation MUST pass the same acceptance
   306	fixtures as gather-feeds-SDPA and MUST be explicitly mode-gated; it MUST NOT
   307	silently replace the v0.1 default.
   308	
   309	### FR-PKV4 — fp16 exactness invariant (SPEC-039-R004)
   310	
   311	For the fp16 KV path, paged KV MUST be numerically exact against the stock
   312	contiguous path for deterministic greedy generation. The acceptance gate is
   313	exact greedy-argmax token parity over at least 32 generated tokens, with KV
   314	exercised on every layer and every decode step. A passing test MUST prove the
   315	paged kernel ran for every K and V cache update under test; a test that
   316	bypasses paged gather is invalid.
   317	
   318	The parity fixtures MUST exercise a **non-degenerate** paged layout, not a
   319	single-block identity case: the context under test MUST span at least two
   320	physical blocks (`>= N` blocks where `N >= 2` for the configured
   321	`block_size_tokens`), the block table MUST use a **non-identity permutation**
   322	(physical block IDs not in ascending logical order), and the 32+ token decode
   323	MUST cross at least one block boundary (a tail block filling and a new block
   324	being allocated mid-decode). A parity pass on a layout that never leaves the
   325	first block, or whose block table is the identity permutation, does not
   326	satisfy this gate.
   327	
   328	The parity fixture set MUST include at least:
   329	
   330	1. a dense Llama-family model;
   331	2. a dense Qwen-family model or documented equivalent second dense
   332	   architecture; and
   333	3. a MoE Qwen3-family model matching the production attention/cache shape.
   334	
   335	Any newly admitted model family beyond Llama/Qwen MUST add its own
   336	environment-gated real-model fixture before the family is added to the
   337	attach-time admission allowlist. For v0.1.2, the only additional admitted
   338	family is `gpt_oss`, with a fixture over `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-Q8`; `gemma4`,
   339	`glm4_moe`, `nemotron_h`, and other catalog families remain outside the
   340	allowlist until they have equivalent FR-PKV4 evidence.
   341	
   342	The implementation MUST fail closed if parity is not established for a model
   343	or cache class selected for paged mode. Tolerance-based tensor comparison MAY
   344	be used as a diagnostic, but it is not a substitute for exact greedy token
   345	parity in the acceptance gate.
   346	
   347	### FR-PKV5 — KV dtype scope and quantized-KV boundary (SPEC-039-R005)
   348	
   349	The v0.1 normative and production path is fp16 KV, matching provider behavior
   350	when `kv_bits` is unset. Paged fp16 KV MUST target fp16 stock SDPA parity.
   351	
   352	Quantized KV is out of scope for v0.1. A future paged-quantized cache MUST
   353	target the quantized numerical surface, not fp16. It MUST conform to the
   354	relevant quantized cache protocol, feed `quantizedScaledDotProductAttention`,
   355	and gather quantized block tuples `(wq, scales, biases)` or their exact
   356	library-equivalent representation. It MUST NOT reinterpret quantized K/V as
   357	plain fp16 tensors, silently disable requested `kvBits`, or claim fp16 parity
   358	as proof of quantized correctness.
   359	
   360	If an operator enables paged KV while `kvBits` is configured before a
   361	quantized paged path exists, the provider MUST route to the stock contiguous
   362	path or fail preflight with an observable reason-coded result. Silent
   363	quantization downgrade is forbidden.
   364	
   365	### FR-PKV6 — provider-local default-off invariants (SPEC-039-R006)
   366	
   367	Paged KV MUST be disabled by default. When disabled, provider behavior MUST
   368	match the stock contiguous path in request schemas, response schemas, receipt
   369	field set, usage computation, billing arithmetic, advertised model identity,
   370	and observable buyer semantics.
   371	
   372	When enabled, paged KV remains provider-local. It MUST NOT add a SPEC-015
   373	receipt field, alter any existing SPEC-015 field computation, add a usage
   374	field, change SPEC-024 `cached_prompt_tokens` semantics, alter SPEC-005
   375	billing arithmetic, or expose block-table/kernel/cache-mode identity to
   376	buyers. Non-receipt operator diagnostics MAY expose paged-mode status,
   377	allocator capacity, fallback counts, and parity/packaging gate state.
   378	
   379	The implementation MUST preserve served model identity: `model_sha256`,
   380	served model ID, tokenizer identity, chat-template identity, and cache-class
   381	compatibility metadata used by SPEC-010/SPEC-024/SPEC-037 gates. If paged
   382	activation misses any compatibility or correctness gate, the provider MUST
   383	fall back to the stock contiguous path or fail preflight before serving the
   384	request in paged mode.
   385	
   386	### FR-PKV7 — fail-safe fallback and observability (SPEC-039-R007)
   387	
   388	Paged mode MUST be fail-safe. Any paged allocator, block-table validation,
   389	kernel registration, kernel dispatch, metallib loading, model compatibility,
   390	pool-capacity, or parity-gate failure MUST NOT corrupt resident stock cache
   391	state and MUST NOT emit a buyer-visible partial response that mixes paged and
   392	stock state.
   393	
   394	For permissive policy, the runtime MAY route the affected request or resident
   395	model to the stock contiguous path. For strict policy, it MAY fail preflight.
   396	Both branches MUST emit an operator-observable, reason-coded result. A
   397	configured paged mode MUST NOT silently become stock contiguous without such
   398	operator observability.
   399	
   400	**Fallback is a preflight / pre-first-token decision.** Reason-coded
   401	stock-contiguous fallback and preflight rejection apply **before any
   402	buyer-visible token, SSE frame, usage accounting, or receipt state** is
   403	emitted for the request. There is no mid-stream fallback: once a request has
   404	emitted its first token in paged mode, a subsequent engine failure MUST fail
   405	the request closed through the normal terminal path and MUST NOT stitch paged
   406	and stock output for one request. Because batch-1 pool footprint is fully
   407	reserved at preflight (FR-PKV2), block-pool exhaustion cannot arise mid-stream
   408	at batch size 1; multi-row shared-pool pressure is a SPEC-038 scheduler
   409	concern.
   410	
   411	Fallback MUST preserve cache isolation: paged physical blocks that were
   412	allocated for a rejected or fallback-routed sequence MUST be reclaimed before
   413	the sequence can be admitted again.
   414	
   415	**Closed reason-code enum (exhaustive, normative — like SPEC-037 FR-KVP12).**
   416	Every paged-mode fail-safe or fallback outcome MUST map to exactly one code in
   417	this closed list; the IMPL MUST NOT invent additional codes without a SPEC
   418	revision:
   419	
   420	- `paged_fallback_cache_class` — cache class / `kv_bits` not on the paged
   421	  allowlist (FR-PKV12);
   422	- `paged_fallback_allocator` — allocation/block-table validation failure or
   423	  pool exhaustion at preflight (FR-PKV2);
   424	- `paged_fallback_kernel` — Metal kernel registration or dispatch failure
   425	  (FR-PKV3);
   426	- `paged_fallback_metallib` — the packaged MLX metallib (`mlx.metallib` or
   427	  `mlx-swift_Cmlx.bundle/Contents/Resources/default.metallib`) missing,
   428	  version-mismatched, or undiscoverable (FR-PKV8);
   429	- `paged_fallback_parity` — a required parity gate is not established for the
   430	  selected model/cache class (FR-PKV4);
   500	
   501	Both operations MUST preserve **SPEC-024 token-granular LCP/trim semantics
   502	exactly**: an extracted or reattached cache MUST support token-granular trim
   503	where every KV layer trims exactly the requested count (a shortfall is a miss,
   504	SPEC-024 FR-CI2/FR-CI3), including a trim at a **mid-block** boundary (the tail
   505	block's valid-token count is adjusted, no whole-block rounding). These
   506	operations are **same-conversation only**: they MUST NOT share, expose, or
   507	reattach one conversation's blocks to a different conversation (the
   508	cross-conversation exclusion in §1 stands), and they grant no buyer-controlled
   509	residency.
   510	
   511	**No broader sharing by implication.** FR-PKV10 is not a salted-prefix,
   512	cross-buyer, cross-account, global content-addressed, or LRU prefix-cache
   513	sharing authority. A future broader prefix-sharing design MUST define, in a
   514	SPEC revision before implementation, the tenant/account scope, salt/key
   515	derivation, hit/miss attribution, purge propagation, privacy disclosure,
   516	receipt/billing effect, and diagnostic observability. Until that exists, any
   517	attempt to reattach or expose blocks outside the same conversation MUST fail
   518	closed before serving.
   519	
   520	### FR-PKV11 — capability descriptor handshake (SPEC-039-R011)
   521	
   522	The engine MUST advertise a **machine-readable capability descriptor** that a
   523	consumer reads to decide whether a requested tuple can be served in paged mode.
   524	The descriptor MUST include at least: `block_size_tokens`, supported model
   525	families, the **allowed cache classes** (the FR-PKV12 allowlist), KV dtype
   526	(fp16 in v0.1), and whether MoE expert-dispatch-shaped models are supported by
   527	the paged path. The descriptor is the single source of truth for paged
   528	capability: a consumer's activation predicate MUST be `requested tuple ∈
   529	engine-advertised descriptor`, never a separately self-declared support matrix
   530	that could drift from what the engine actually serves. The descriptor MUST be
   531	derivable at attach time and MUST reflect the FR-PKV12 attach-time allowlist
   532	result for the resident model.
   533	
   534	Family identity MUST be derived from the resident model's `config.json`
   535	metadata when available, using `model_type` / `architectures` rather than only
   536	repository-name substrings. Malformed or unknown config metadata MUST NOT
   537	expand support by guesswork: the resident tuple remains outside the descriptor
   538	unless its canonical family label is in the explicit admission allowlist and
   539	all runtime measurement gates pass.
   540	
   541	### FR-PKV12 — cache-class allowlist and attach-time admission gate (SPEC-039-R012)
   542	
   543	At model attach, the engine MUST inspect the runtime `newCache()` class and the
   544	`kv_bits` setting against a **paged allowlist**. The v1 allowlist is:
   545	**non-rotating contiguous `KVCacheSimple`-equivalent, fp16, `kv_bits` unset.**
   546	The sole mixed-layout exception requires the exact `qwen/qwen3.6-27b` serving
   547	identity, `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` in the artifact's `config.json`
   548	architectures, and a runtime cache topology measured as `MambaCache` on
   549	recurrent layers and `KVCacheSimple` on full-attention layers. The engine MUST preserve each row's
   550	Mamba convolution and delta state independently, page only attention KV, and
   551	pass token-parity and multi-step batched row-isolation gates, including row
   552	leave and join, before advertising
   553	the exact tuple. This exception covers first-turn/cache-miss requests only;
   554	retained or positive-cache-credit hybrid requests MUST stay on the serial path
   555	unless the SPEC-038 FR-CB10 accepted tuple covering the requested runtime tuple
   556	records `cached_turns_accepted: true`. That grant is the recurrent-state
   557	handoff's reviewed proof: the SPEC-038 AC-26 packaged proof, including a
   558	checkpoint-resumed turn, on that exact tuple and runtime revision.
   559	A model whose runtime cache class is **not** on the allowlist — enumerated
   560	non-allowlisted classes include `RotatingKVCache` (sliding-window),
   561	`CacheList` (unproven hybrid), and `QuantizedKVCache` — MUST **fail safe to the stock
   562	contiguous path** with an **observable reason code** (`paged_fallback_cache_class`,
   563	FR-PKV7), logged **once at attach**. Paged mode MUST NOT be advertised in the
   564	FR-PKV11 descriptor for a non-allowlisted class.
   565	
   566	This gate is correctness-load-bearing, not merely an optimization guard: the
   567	v0.1 gather-feeds-SDPA path assumes the stock full-context causal mask. Paging
   568	a **sliding-window** (`RotatingKVCache`) model through it would silently defeat
   569	the model's own windowed masking and produce **wrong tokens billed as
   570	correct** — so a non-allowlisted cache class MUST never be served in paged
   571	mode, exactly as SPEC-037 AC-10 fails a non-`KVCacheSimple` family safe to a
   572	miss with an observable skip.
   573	
   574	**Serve-time memory cap vs. model attention type (v0.1.1 clarification).** The
   575	runtime `newCache()` class conflates two independent reasons a model presents a
   576	`RotatingKVCache`: (a) the model's **attention type** genuinely needs windowing
   577	(sliding-window / hybrid), and (b) the **serve path capped KV size** for memory
   578	(`maxKVSize != nil`) on an otherwise **full-context** model, which makes

   580	attention is full-causal and its KV layout is contiguous. Only case (a) is a

   582	inspects MUST therefore be the class the **paged path itself** would use — i.e.
   583	evaluated with the serve memory cap removed (`maxKVSize = nil`), because a paged
   584	row's memory is bounded by the FR-PKV2 block pool, not by KV rotation. A
   585	full-context model that resolves to `KVCacheSimple` uncapped is allowlisted and
   586	attaches (the block pool assumes the memory-bounding role the cap held for the
   587	non-batched serve cache); a model that resolves to `RotatingKVCache` (or another
   588	non-allowlisted class) **even uncapped** genuinely needs windowing/hybrid/
   589	quantized handling and MUST still fail safe with `paged_fallback_cache_class`.

   311	ceiling — that would collapse effective concurrency toward depth 1 — so an
   312	admitted row MAY still exhaust the pool mid-decode and is then resolved by the
   313	deterministic request-local failure path (FR-CB5), never by preemption. This
   314	reconciles the Entry-110 active-row cap (FR-CB11) with real pool state: the cap
   315	is an upper bound on rows, and pool availability is the admission-time gate
   316	underneath it (FR-CB17).
   317	
   318	### FR-CB2 - separate prompt and decode batches, decode-first (SPEC-038-R002)
   319	
   320	The scheduler MUST keep prompt processing (prefill) and decode as separate
   321	phases; it MUST NOT combine arbitrary prefill and one-token decode work into
   322	one heterogeneous model call in v0.2. A request joins the shared decode batch
   323	only after its prompt prefill completes and its request-private block table is
   324	initialized over `SPEC-039` blocks. Scheduling MUST be decode-first: each
   325	iteration advances the current decode batch by a bounded window of `W >= 1`
   326	tokens. Per-row sampling, stop conditions and emission are applied to every
   327	token in order. The iteration then removes terminal rows, processes
   328	cancellation at a safe boundary, and only then admits and prefills new prompt
   329	work into free capacity.
   330	
   331	`W` is capped by each row's remaining output budget and by the configured
   332	lockstep window. It MUST be 1 while a request is waiting for a free slot or
   333	being admitted, so that request joins at the next hop boundary (FR-CB5). While
   334	a prompt is mid-prefill and nothing else is waiting to join, `W` MUST NOT
   335	exceed the prefill decode window. The prefill decode window gives active rows
   336	several tokens per prefill chunk rather than one, so a long prompt slows them
   337	by a bounded factor instead of stalling them. Prefill MUST be bounded or
   338	chunked (one chunk per iteration) so a long prompt cannot block existing
   339	decode rows for an unbounded interval. Prefill never samples, so it evaluates
   340	only the prompt's cache state, not the vocabulary projection.
   341	
   342	This decode-first split is a v0.2 safety choice. It preserves simple
   343	per-request accounting, cancellation, and receipt boundaries while the shared
   344	forward is first enabled. It MUST NOT be described as equivalent to a
   345	unified-token, mixed-phase, priority, or disaggregated-prefill scheduler: those
   346	may improve utilization under mixed prompt lengths, but they are future
   347	optimization work and require new correctness/evidence gates before serving
   348	real traffic.
   349	
   350	### FR-CB3 - one shared forward for active decode rows (SPEC-038-R003)
   351	
   352	Each decode iteration MUST invoke the model once for all active decode rows
   353	together (one shared `[B, 1]`-shaped forward), not as `B` independent model
   354	calls. This shared forward is the defining behavior of the feature; a
   355	configuration that merely runs multiple concurrent iterators is the serial
   356	path, not batching, and MUST NOT be reported as continuous batching in
   357	telemetry (FR-CB14).
   358	
   359	### FR-CB4 - scheduler ownership of per-request block tables (SPEC-038-R004)
   360	
   361	The scheduler MUST own each request's block table lifecycle over the
   362	`SPEC-039` paged engine through the **engine-issued block-table handle**
   363	(SPEC-039 FR-PKV2). The verb **"allocate" is reserved for the engine**: the
   364	scheduler MUST **request allocation of, bind, extend, release-completed-rows,
   365	detach, and release** request block-table mappings only at scheduler-owned
   366	lifecycle boundaries: admission, prefill completion, decode-step completion,
   367	cancellation, terminal stop, request-local failure, batch-level failure, cache
   368	commit, and warm-swap drain. The scheduler MUST NOT expose one request's block
   369	table, cache handle, or logical token positions to another request. The
   370	scheduler MUST NOT redefine `SPEC-039` storage layout, block size,
   371	paged-attention kernel semantics, or allocator internals; it consumes only the
   372	capability the engine advertises in its **capability descriptor** (SPEC-039
   373	FR-PKV11). Per-request extraction back into standalone conversation-cache state
   374	MUST use the SPEC-039 **cache-extraction / same-conversation retention
   375	primitive** (SPEC-039 FR-PKV10) and MUST preserve exact SPEC-024 LCP/trim
   376	semantics (including a mid-block LCP boundary).
   377	
   378	For a hybrid model (paged attention plus recurrent layers), whose recurrent
   379	state cannot be retained or trimmed as paged KV, a conversation-keyed batched
   380	row with zero cached tokens MUST end a prefill chunk exactly on each SPEC-024
   381	FR-CI2 recurrent checkpoint position (at most two) and snapshot only its own
   382	recurrent-layer state there. At a normal terminal (stop or length), before
   383	releasing its blocks, it MUST commit a serial-format conversation-cache entry:
   384	its attention KV materialized through FR-PKV10 into contiguous caches covering
   385	a prefix of the canonical token list (prompt plus generated tokens, trailing
   386	model stop dropped), and the snapshots as that entry's recurrent checkpoints.
   387	Keyless, cancelled and failed rows MUST commit nothing and MUST release every
   388	block and snapshot they hold. A later turn with positive
   389	`cached_prompt_tokens` still serial-routes until AC-26.
   390	
   440	participating request, and that batch-level failure path MUST perform
   441	deterministic cleanup (FR-CB7).
   442	
   443	A **mid-decode block-extension failure** — an active decode row cannot extend
   444	its block table because the shared paged pool is exhausted — is a
   445	**request-local, deterministic failure of that row only** (FR-CB17): it fails
   446	that row through the request-local terminal path, releases the row's blocks,
   447	and leaves every other row's stream, sampler, stop state, and block table
   448	intact. It is **not** a whole-batch failure and **not** true preemption
   449	(evict-and-recompute); v0.2 does not preempt (FR-CB16, FR-CB17). Admission
   450	back-pressure (FR-CB1) is the primary defense that makes this path rare.
   451	
   452	### FR-CB6 - per-request isolation under the shared forward (SPEC-038-R006)
   453	
   454	This is the load-bearing invariant. Under one shared forward the scheduler
   455	MUST guarantee, per request:
   456	
   457	- exactly one terminal result per accepted request;
   458	- no token attributed to the wrong request;
   459	- no cross-request sampler state, stop-sequence state, or logit-processor
   460	  state;
   461	- no cross-request conversation-cache or block-table exposure;
   462	- per-request `prompt_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_prompt_tokens`, and
   463	  terminal status computed exactly as on the serial path;
   464	- the receipt built for each request preserving the LOCKED SPEC-015
   465	  per-request field set and computation rules, with no batch identifier in
   466	  the receipt identity tuple.
   467	
   468	Batch metadata (row index, batch depth, mean fill, cohort) MAY appear only in
   469	non-receipt diagnostic telemetry (FR-CB14) and MUST NOT alter buyer-visible
   470	token accounting. Deterministic (temperature-0) output for a request under
   471	batching MUST match its serial-path output within the accepted numerical
   472	tolerance.
   473	
   474	A sampled (non-greedy) request MAY batch. Its row MUST select each token with
   475	exactly the sampling algorithm the serial path uses for the same request
   476	parameters (temperature, top_p), applied only to that row's own logits. The
   477	row's randomness MUST be row-local:
   478	- it is derived from that request's identity and the step index;
   479	- it is never shared with another row;
   480	- it is never carried in hidden cross-step state.
   481	
   482	Sampled output is therefore equal in distribution to the serial path, not
   483	token-identical to a particular serial run (the serial path is not seeded). A
   484	replay of the same request identity reproduces the same draws. Parameters the
   485	serial path ignores (presence and frequency penalties) MUST be ignored on the
   486	batched path too, so batching never changes what a request asks for.
   487	
   488	The accepted numerical tolerance recognizes that a shared batched forward and
   489	a serial forward differ only in floating-point ACCUMULATION ORDER (batched
   490	matmuls and MoE expert routing versus a single row), which can flip greedy
   491	argmax between two near-tied tokens of the SAME request's own distribution. For
   492	the load-time batched isolation self-test (the MoE input-isolation probe), a
   493	row's greedy token is therefore conformant when it is EITHER the row's own
   494	serial-path argmax, OR the row's own serial-path runner-up whose logit is within
   495	a fixed small tolerance of that row's serial argmax logit — a genuine
   496	own-distribution numerical tie. Any other token is a divergence; in particular a
   497	token equal to ANOTHER row's serial argmax MUST always be treated as a
   498	divergence (a leak), never as a tie. This tolerance applies ONLY to the
   499	batched-versus-serial argmax comparison; it does NOT relax the SPEC-039 single-
   500	row paged-gather parity gate, which shares the serial computation's accumulation
   501	order and so remains exact.
   502	
   503	### FR-CB7 - single-owner actor isolation (SPEC-038-R007)
   504	
   505	All mutable batch state (queue, prompt set, decode batch, per-row lifecycle,
   506	request block tables, cache handles, admission reservations, and terminal
   507	bookkeeping) MUST be owned by a single Swift actor or an equivalently
   508	single-owner isolation domain. Supported batched rows and unsupported
   509	independent serial iterators MUST NOT run against the same resident model
   510	concurrently without a proof of thread safety. Cancellation MUST be observed
   511	at a bounded scheduler boundary. Cleanup after a batch-level failure MUST be
   512	deterministic.
   513	
   514	### FR-CB8 - explicit rejection of unsupported cache / kv_bits modes (SPEC-038-R008)
   515	
   516	The scheduler's support determination MUST be `requested tuple ∈
   517	engine-advertised descriptor`: it reads the **SPEC-039 capability descriptor**
   518	(FR-PKV11 — block size, supported model families, allowed cache classes, KV
   519	dtype, MoE-dispatch support) and admits a tuple to batching only when the
   520	descriptor advertises it. The scheduler MUST NOT maintain a separately
   521	self-declared support matrix that could drift from what the engine actually
   522	serves. For a cache class, `SPEC-039` capability, MoE/expert-dispatch surface,
   523	or quantized-KV (`kv_bits`) configuration **outside** the engine-advertised
   524	descriptor, the runtime MUST either route the request to the serial path when
   525	policy permits, or fail preflight with an observable, reason-coded error. It MUST NOT silently disable

   210	The engine MUST store K/V in fixed-size physical blocks managed by a
   211	provider-local allocator. A v0.1 implementation MUST define one configured
   212	`block_size_tokens` for a resident cache pool at activation time; all
   213	sequences in that pool use the same block size until the pool is recreated.
   214	The block size MUST be a positive integer selected before serving begins and
   215	recorded in compatibility metadata for tests, telemetry, and any persistence
   216	consumer.
   217	
   218	Each resident paged pool MUST also have a hard configured capacity, expressed
   219	as `max_physical_blocks`, `max_pool_bytes`, or an equivalent bound from which
   220	both are derivable. The capacity MUST be selected before serving begins,
   221	recorded in diagnostics and acceptance fixtures, and enforced before request
   222	admission or GPU dispatch. The allocator MUST reserve the blocks needed for a
   223	sequence extension before that extension can become buyer-visible. Capacity
   224	exhaustion MUST produce a reason-coded preflight failure or stock-contiguous
   225	fallback before any partial response, usage accounting, receipt construction,
   226	or unreclaimable paged state is emitted. It MUST NOT rely on Swift, MLX, or
   227	Metal out-of-memory failure as the capacity-control mechanism.
   228	
   229	For every active sequence, the block table MUST map logical block indices
   230	`0..<ceil(sequence_kv_tokens / block_size_tokens)` to physical block IDs in
   231	logical order. The last logical block MUST carry the count of valid tokens.
   232	Attention code MUST treat bytes beyond that valid-token count as unreadable
   233	padding. A block table with a missing physical block, duplicated physical
   234	block for writable sequence state, out-of-range block ID, negative logical
   235	length, or valid-token count outside `1...block_size_tokens` for a non-empty
   236	tail MUST be rejected before GPU dispatch.
   237	
   238	The allocator MUST maintain an explicit free list or equivalent exact free
   239	set, allocate whole physical blocks, and reclaim whole physical blocks only
   240	after no live sequence table references them. Reclaim is **mechanism only**:
   241	the engine MUST NOT reclaim any physical block that is referenced by an
   242	in-flight decode step, and the eviction/reclaim **policy** (which sequence's
   243	blocks to reclaim under pressure, and when) is deferred to the consumer —
   244	SPEC-038 owns it under batching. The engine exposes eviction as a
   245	sequence-scoped mechanism only, unless a future SPEC defines safe subsequence
   246	or shared-prefix ownership. A failed allocation MUST either trigger a
   247	reason-coded fallback to the stock contiguous path before paged state becomes
   248	visible, or fail preflight with a reason-coded error; it MUST NOT produce
   249	partial paged state.
   250	
   251	**Ownership boundary (engine vs. consumer).** The engine owns physical-block
   252	allocation, the free list, block-table validation, and issues block IDs and a
   253	per-sequence block-table handle; the verb **"allocate"** is reserved for the
   254	engine. A consumer (e.g. the SPEC-038 scheduler) owns the per-request
   255	logical→physical mapping *lifecycle* — request allocation, bind, extend,
   256	release — through the engine-issued handle; it MUST NOT reach past the handle
   257	into free-list or block-storage internals.
   258	
   259	**Concurrency model.** All allocator state transitions (allocate, free,
   260	reclaim, block-table validation) MUST be serialized by a single-driver
   261	isolation domain (a single Swift actor or equivalent single-owner domain), so
   262	no two callers mutate the free list or a block table concurrently.
   263	
   264	**Batch-size-1 pool sizing (mid-stream exhaustion structurally impossible).**
   265	At batch size 1 the resident paged pool capacity MUST be `>=` the worst-case
   266	single-sequence context the request may reach: admission MUST reject at
   267	preflight (reason-coded) when the request's `max_tokens` (prompt + generated
   268	ceiling) cannot be guaranteed to fit within the pool for that lone sequence.
   269	Because the whole worst-case footprint is reserved at preflight, a batch-1
   270	sequence can never run out of blocks mid-decode; block-pool exhaustion is a
   271	preflight/pre-first-token condition, not a mid-stream one (FR-PKV7). Behavior
   272	of block-extension failure under a *shared* pool with multiple rows is a
   273	SPEC-038 scheduler concern (admission back-pressure plus request-local
   274	failure), not an engine mid-stream partial-response path.

   276	### FR-PKV3 — paged-attention kernel modes (SPEC-039-R003)
   277	
   278	The v0.1 normative proof mode is **gather-feeds-SDPA**. The implementation
   279	MUST register a custom Metal kernel through public `MLXFast.metalKernel` that

   285	stock fp16 KV path.

   621	These are normative define-and-record obligations; the specific byte and

   624	
   625	The overhead ceiling is enforced per tuple through SPEC-038 FR-CB10 acceptance
   626	coverage, not by a startup micro-benchmark. A throughput measurement at

   649	
   650	Default-off invariants are FR-PKV6; the fallback-policy values select the

   655	
   656	| Configuration | Required result |
   657	|---|---|
   658	| Paged flag off | Stock contiguous path; no buyer-visible behavior change. |

   660	| Paged flag on, non-allowlisted cache class at attach (`RotatingKVCache`/sliding-window, `CacheList`/hybrid, `QuantizedKVCache`) | Fail safe to stock contiguous with `paged_fallback_cache_class`, logged once at attach; paged not advertised in descriptor (FR-PKV12). |

   663	| Paged flag on, `kvBits` configured and no paged-quantized path exists | Reason-coded stock fallback or preflight failure; no silent quantization downgrade. |

   665	| Gather-feeds-SDPA exact parity passes, but overhead ceiling fails | Valid correctness/parity evidence only; paged mode MUST NOT serve real traffic through that path for the tuple. |

   667	| Fully-fused op configured | Explicit mode-gated extension; must pass all fp16 parity fixtures before use. |

 # Issue #191: write the inlined watchdog.sh to disk.
 #
 # IMPORTANT: the body below must stay byte-identical (after comment

   write_atomic_install_file "$WATCHDOG_PATH" 0755 <<'WATCHDOG_EOF'
 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 # macprovider-watchdog: local provider liveness monitor.
 #
 # Health verdict: the exact launchd service PID must own the configured local
 # listener and its /v1/health endpoint must answer. /v1/health returns non-2xx
 # for degraded/draining/unavailable states, so a provider stuck reporting
 # unavailable after the watchdog is armed is restartable. Coordinator TCP
 # reachability is advisory logging only; a missing ESTABLISHED coordinator

index 016b6dc46..ca91b5bf1 100644

@@ -29,23 +29,23 @@
   <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
   <string>__LOG_DIR__/macprovider.err.log</string>

   <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
   <dict>
     <key>HOME</key>
     <string>__USER_HOME__</string>
     <key>PATH</key>

diff --git a/phase3-binary/dist/test/install_prefix.test.sh b/phase3-binary/dist/test/install_prefix.test.sh
index f9db35e35..3033d4a99 100755
--- a/phase3-binary/dist/test/install_prefix.test.sh
+++ b/phase3-binary/dist/test/install_prefix.test.sh
@@ -23,21 +23,32 @@ HEADLESS_USER=""
 LAUNCHD_DOMAIN="gui/$UID"
 mkdir -p "$HOME"
 
 # shellcheck source=/dev/null
 source "$TMP/render.sh"
 plist="$(render_plist 'mlx-community/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-4bit' 'provider-1' 'wss://coordinator.malibu.tech/ws/provider')"
 
 printf "%s\n" "$plist" | grep -A1 '<key>WorkingDirectory</key>' | grep -F '<string>/opt/mp</string>' >/dev/null
 printf "%s\n" "$plist" | grep -A8 '<key>ProgramArguments</key>' | grep -F '<string>serve</string>' >/dev/null
 printf "%s\n" "$plist" | grep -A8 '<key>ProgramArguments</key>' | grep -F '<string>--config</string>' >/dev/null
 printf "%s\n" "$plist" | grep -A8 '<key>ProgramArguments</key>' | grep -F "<string>$CONFIG_PATH</string>" >/dev/null
 if printf "%s\n" "$plist" | grep -Eq '<string>--(model|provider-id|coordinator|port)</string>'; then
   echo "mutable provider settings leaked into launchd ProgramArguments" >&2
   exit 1
 fi
 grep -F '<string>__CONFIG_PATH__</string>' "$PLIST_TEMPLATE" >/dev/null
 if grep -Eq '<string>--(model|provider-id|coordinator|port)</string>' "$PLIST_TEMPLATE"; then
   echo "mutable provider settings leaked into launchd template ProgramArguments" >&2
   exit 1
 fi
+# SPEC-003 v0.11.4: launchd pins `Adaptive`/`Background` jobs at background
+# priority, which costs about 40% of decode throughput. The provider must be
+# `Standard` in the rendered plist and in both shipped templates.
+COMPAT_TEMPLATE="$REPO_ROOT/phase3-binary/dist/compatibility-set-assets/provider-launch-agent.plist.template"
+printf "%s\n" "$plist" | grep -A1 '<key>ProcessType</key>' | grep -F '<string>Standard</string>' >/dev/null
+for template in "$PLIST_TEMPLATE" "$COMPAT_TEMPLATE"; do
+  if ! grep -A1 '<key>ProcessType</key>' "$template" | grep -F '<string>Standard</string>' >/dev/null; then
+    echo "provider launchd template must use ProcessType Standard: $template" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+done

+/// Pure block/capacity arithmetic for `PagedKVCache` storage, kept free of MLX
+/// so it is testable on hosts without the Metal library.
+enum PagedKVBlockLayout {
+    /// Growth step, matching `KVCacheSimple.step`.
+    static let growthStepTokens = 256
+    static func blockCount(tokens: Int, blockSizeTokens: Int) -> Int {
+        guard tokens > 0, blockSizeTokens > 0 else { return 0 }
+        return (tokens - 1) / blockSizeTokens + 1
+    }
+    /// Half-open token ranges of each logical block over `tokens` stored tokens;
+    /// every block is full except possibly the last.
+    static func blockRanges(tokens: Int, blockSizeTokens: Int) -> [Range<Int>] {
+        (0 ..< blockCount(tokens: tokens, blockSizeTokens: blockSizeTokens)).map { index in
+            let start = index * blockSizeTokens
+            return start ..< min(start + blockSizeTokens, tokens)
+        }
+    }
+    /// Capacity after growing a buffer holding `stored` tokens so it fits
+    /// `needed`: whole growth steps past `stored`, never above `maxTokens`
+    /// unless `needed` itself is larger (callers reject that case first).
+    static func grownCapacity(
+        stored: Int,
+        needed: Int,
+        maxTokens: Int,
+        step: Int = growthStepTokens

+        let steps = (step + incoming - 1) / step

+        let (capacity, capacityOverflow) = stored.addingReportingOverflow(growth)
+        let bounded = growthOverflow || capacityOverflow ? maxTokens : min(capacity, maxTokens)
+        return max(needed, bounded)
+    }

 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	# Qwen3.6 throughput decomposition on the Mac Studio (2026-09-25)
     2	
     3	Question: why does Qwen3.6-27B serve at about 15 tok/s under continuous
     4	batching (CB) on a 256 GB M3 Ultra, when 100 tok/s was expected?
     5	
     6	## Physics
     7	
     8	- **Serial decode: 36–38 tok/s at every context length.** This is close to the
     9	  bandwidth ceiling: about 15 GB of weights are read per token at about
    10	  819 GB/s. A single stream cannot reach 100 tok/s.
    11	- **100 tok/s is an aggregate target.** Only batching can reach it, because one
    12	  weight read then serves several rows.
    13	- **Prefill runs at about 300 tok/s serial,** so a 4k-token prompt takes about
    14	  14 s before its first token.
    15	
    16	## Before (`b0f3d45f`): batched decode lost to serial at long context
    17	
    18	Steady-state aggregate decode, measured only over the window where every row is
    19	decoding (`steady_decode.py`):
    20	
    21	| Prompt × rows | tok/s |
    22	| --- | --- |
    23	| 32 × 4 | 54.8 |
    24	| 1.5k × 2 | 36.8 |
    25	| 1.5k × 4 | 43.2 |
    26	| 3k × 3 | 29.1 |
    27	| 4k × 4 | 28.1 |
    28	
    29	The profile (`profile-steady-decode-3x3072.txt`) showed
    30	`PagedKVCache.update` doing this on every decode step:
    31	
    32	- re-concatenating the row's whole K/V history;
    33	- re-splitting it into blocks.
    34	
    35	That made each step O(context).
    36	
    37	## Fix (`3a91f1bc`): in-place paged-KV writes
    38	
    39	- Each layer keeps contiguous `[B,H,capacity,D]` backing buffers. They grow in
    40	  256-token steps, capped at `maxResidentTokens`.
    41	- New tokens are written with slice assignment.
    42	- Block views are derived on demand, and `trim` is O(1).
    43	- Output is byte-identical to the old path on a random-weight model locally, and
    44	  all 3439 package tests pass.
    45	
    46	## After (`3a91f1bc`, binary `e45d3a983cb77ef6`)
    47	
    48	Data: [`data/cb-perf-2026-09-25/after-o1/`](data/cb-perf-2026-09-25/after-o1/).
    49	
    50	### Steady-state batched decode
    51	
    52	| Prompt × rows | Before | After |
    53	| --- | --- | --- |
    54	| 32 × 4 | 54.8 | **67.6** |
    55	| 1.5k × 2 | 36.8 | **54.7** |
    56	| 1.5k × 4 | 43.2 | **64.0** |
    57	| 4k × 1 serial | 36.4 | 36.4 |
    58	
    59	Batched decode now reaches 1.5–1.75× serial, and the drop from 32 to 1.5k
    60	tokens of context is small.
    61	
    62	At 4k × 4 and 8k × 4 no steady window exists: the first row finishes 768
    63	tokens before the last row's prefill ends. See the next section.
    64	
    65	### End to end (128 output tokens, `matrix.jsonl`)
    66	
    67	| Prompt × rows | Aggregate tok/s | Worst first token | Prefill per row |
    68	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    69	| 512 × 4 | 36.4 | 9.3 s | 110 tok/s |
    70	| 1.5k × 4 | 19.9 | 25.0 s | 117 tok/s |
    71	| 4k × 4 | 8.8 | 69.6 s | 117 tok/s |
    72	
    73	End to end, prefill dominates:
    74	
    75	- The scheduler admits one prefill per iteration, and the prefill chunks of
    76	  that one row alternate with decode steps.
    77	- Per-row prefill drops from about 300 tok/s serial to about 117 tok/s under
    78	  load.
    79	- Rows queue behind each other's prompts.
    80	
    81	The remaining gap to 100 tok/s is prefill scheduling, not decode.
    82	
    83	### Correctness
    84	
    85	- **Startup probes:** parity `established=true`; batched isolation proven with
    86	  0 cross-row divergences.
    87	- **`isolate_q36`:** 5 of 5 scenarios, every row exact.
    88	- **`crossrow_q36` (greedy, compared against serial):**
    89	  - n=2 and n=4: every row exact.
    90	  - n=8: 7 of 8 rows exact. The eighth diverges at char 83 with no leak signal,
    91	    which is the FR-CB6 accumulation-order tolerance.
    92	- **Failures:** 0 `batching_forward_failed` or `batching_prefill_failed` events.
    93	
    94	## MLX ceiling: the model-level harness (`msb-throughput`, same binary)
    95	
    96	This measures aggregate decode for N rows, with no scheduler, HTTP or prefill
    97	involved. Runs used 128 decode tokens. Data:
    98	[`data/cb-perf-2026-09-25/msb-scale/`](data/cb-perf-2026-09-25/msb-scale/).
    99	
   100	| Rows | Stock MLX contiguous KV, L=32 | Stock MLX, L=1.5k | Our paged engine, L=32 | Our paged engine, L=1.5k |
   101	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   102	| 1 | 37.2 | 38.0 | 34.2 | 34.5 |
   103	| 2 | 59.7 | 63.1 | 56.6 | 57.3 |
   104	| 4 | 70.6 | 72.6 | 66.4 | 68.0 |
   105	| 8 | 78.7 | 81.3 | 76.1 | 79.1 |
   106	
   107	- **Stock MLX peaks at about 80 tok/s at 8 rows** for this 4-bit 27B hybrid
   108	  model. The stock engine is a plain `KVCacheSimple` with a batch dimension,
   109	  compiled.
   110	- **Our paged engine is now within 3–6% of that ceiling.** The serve's
   111	  steady-state 64.0 tok/s at 1.5k × 4 is within about 6% of the harness figure
   112	  of 68.0.
   113	- **Where the limit comes from:** past about 4 rows, per-step cost grows almost
   114	  linearly with rows. This is a property of MLX's small-batch quantized matmul
   115	  and the gated-delta recurrent layers, not of our scheduler or cache.
   116	- **What 100 tok/s would need:** more than 8 rows, or kernel-level work in MLX.
   117	
   118	## Where the "15 tok/s" comes from
   119	
   120	Take a typical agent request: a ~1.5k-token prompt and ~150 output tokens.
   121	
   122	- Prefill takes about 5 s at the compute-bound ~300 tok/s.
   123	- Decode takes about 4 s.
   124	
   125	Per request that is about 16 output tok/s, which matches what buyers see. The
   126	dominant cost is prefill, and prefill is compute-bound: about 54 GFLOP per token
   127	× 300 tok/s ≈ 16 TFLOPS on the M3 Ultra.
   128	
   129	The levers that move it:
   130	
   131	- **Prefix and conversation reuse.** M4 turned a 76.6 s re-prefill into a 1.0 s
   132	  follow-up.
   133	- **Enough concurrency to fill 8 rows.**
   134	- **Prefill/decode fairness,** so prompts do not stall other rows.
   135	
   136	## Production decodes at 20.5 tok/s because launchd runs it at background priority
   137	
   138	Production v1.8.192 measures about 20.5 tok/s single-stream decode, while the
   139	campaign serve measures 36.4. Data:
   140	[`data/cb-perf-2026-09-25/process-type/`](data/cb-perf-2026-09-25/process-type/).
   141	
   142	| Process | Priority | Decode tok/s (768 tokens, serial) |
   143	| --- | --- | --- |
   144	| Live `:8080` (launchd, `ProcessType` `Adaptive`) | 4 | 22.3–23.4 |
   145	| v1.8.192 release binary, shell launch | normal | 37.7 |
   146	| Same binary under `taskpolicy -b` | 4 | 22.1 |
   147	| Same binary, launchd `ProcessType` `Adaptive` | 4 | 22.3 |
   148	| Same binary, launchd `ProcessType` `Standard` | 20 | **37.8** |
   149	| Lab binary with the live `max_context_override` of 200000 | normal | 37.7 |
   150	
   151	What this rules out, and what it shows:
   152	
   153	- **Not the binary, the config, the context setting or the measurement.** The
   154	  release binary at normal priority decodes as fast as the campaign build.
   155	- **The cause is launchd priority.** launchd leaves an `Adaptive` job at
   156	  background priority unless XPC activity boosts it, and a network daemon never
   157	  gets that boost. The `Background` value that SPEC-003 specified behaves the
   158	  same way.
   159	- **Why priority matters here.** Decode issues many small Metal command
   160	  buffers per token, and background QoS throttles the CPU threads that encode
   161	  and commit them.
   162	
   163	Fix, SPEC-003 v0.11.4: the provider LaunchAgent uses `ProcessType` `Standard`
   164	in all three sources: `install.sh`, `launchd-plist-template.plist` and the
   165	signed compatibility-set template that auto-update renders.
   166	
   167	## Next
   168	
   169	Prefill scheduling:
   170	
   171	- Prefill several admitted rows together.
   172	- Give prefill a token budget per iteration, so a long prompt cannot starve
   173	  decode rows or queue other prompts behind it.
   174	
   175	Then profile the hybrid prefill kernel itself, which runs at about 300 tok/s
   176	serial.
